summary.text: Joe Tache, a Party for Socialism and Liberation candidate and Boston youth worker and community organizer, lost the November 3, 2026 election for U.S. Senate in Massachusetts to Ed Markey.
He is a Philadelphia native who attended Northeastern University, where he studied business.

paragraphs.text: Joe Tache is a Philadelphia native who attended Northeastern University, where he studied business.

While at Northeastern he took part in marches and protests against police brutality and gentrification, for housing justice and alongside campus dining hall workers in a contract dispute, and he says the experience led him to identify with socialism.
Tache works as a youth worker and community organizer in Boston; WAMC described him in September 2026 as a 31-year-old community organizer and activist from Boston.
He ran for the seat Ed Markey has held since 2013 and appeared on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot.

He described his campaign as a socialist alternative to both major parties, and it called for redistributing wealth, a 90% cut to the military budget and public funding of housing, healthcare and education.
He received 2.2% of the vote to Ed Markey's 63.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
